subject: System Design
title: Certificates and Certificate Authorities
description: A short lesson to help you apply Certificates and Certificate Authorities.

hook.text: How does your browser know it's really talking to google.com and not an impostor?

buildup.text: TLS certificates prove a server's identity. They're issued by trusted Certificate Authorities.

discovery.text: Your browser has a built-in list of trusted CAs. If a certificate chains back to one, it's trusted.

twist.text: A compromised CA can issue fake certificates for any domain. This has happened — DigiNotar was hacked in 2011.

climax.text: Certificate Transparency logs now publicly record every issued certificate, making rogue certificates detectable.

punchline.text: Certificates prove identity; CAs vouch for them.
